D: A reluctant officer dropped into an alien war keeps waking on the same day, and has to train until he gets it right.
P: Serve the snacks when Cage wakes up face down at Heathrow, again.
S: waking at the army base at Heathrow every morning
Thick bacon rashers fried crisp, stuffed into soft white rolls with butter and brown sauce, wrapped in paper for the next drop.
Mussels steamed open in white wine with garlic, eschalot and parsley, finished with butter, served with crusty bread to mop up.
Same day again pork and fennel rolls
living the same day over and over

Pork mince with onion, sage and fennel seed rolled in puff pastry, egg washed and baked golden, cut into pieces and served hot with tomato relish. Mix 500g pork mince with a grated onion, 1 tbsp chopped sage, 1 tsp crushed fennel seeds, 30g breadcrumbs, salt and pepper. Halve 2 puff pastry sheets, lay a log of filling along each strip, roll up and seal with beaten egg. Cut each into 4, brush with egg and score the tops. Bake at 200C for 25 minutes until golden and puffed. Serve hot with tomato relish.
M: Farmhouse chicken, bacon and leek stew
the farmhouse where Cage and Rita hide out

Chicken thighs, smoky bacon, leeks and potatoes simmered in stock with thyme until thick, grain mustard and cream stirred through, with crusty bread. Brown 1kg chicken thighs cut into chunks and 150g diced smoked bacon. Add 2 sliced leeks and cook 5 minutes until soft. Stir in 1 tbsp flour, then 750ml chicken stock, 600g potatoes in chunks and thyme. Simmer 35 minutes until thick and the potatoes are tender. Stir in 2 tbsp wholegrain mustard and 100ml cream. Season and serve with crusty bread.
Normandy chicken with cider and cream
the beach landing, again and again

Chicken thighs browned and braised in apple cider with eschalots and mushrooms, finished with cream and parsley, with a warm baguette to mop the sauce. Season 1kg chicken thighs and brown in butter for 4 minutes a side, then set aside. Soften 2 sliced eschalots and 200g sliced mushrooms in the pan. Pour in 375ml apple cider and scrape up the browned bits. Return the chicken, cover and simmer 25 minutes. Stir in 150ml cream and simmer 3 minutes until glossy. Scatter with parsley and serve with a warm baguette.
W: the mess hall at the forward base
Date sponge baked at 180C for 35 minutes, soaked with a butterscotch sauce of brown sugar, butter and cream, served warm with custard.
K: Gunfire: army tea with dark rum

Old British army brew of strong black tea stewed in a big pot, sweetened with brown sugar and milk, with a tot of dark rum in each mug. Warm a big teapot with boiling water and tip it out. Add 6 black tea bags and 1.2L freshly boiled water and leave to stew for 5 minutes until properly strong. Put 2 tsp brown sugar and 30ml dark rum into each of four metal mugs. Pour in the tea, add a splash of milk and stir well.

s.note: waking at the army base at Heathrow every morning
s.how: Fry 8 thick rashers of bacon until crisp at the edges. Split 4 soft white rolls and butter them generously. Stuff two rashers into each roll with a good squeeze of brown sauce, then wrap tightly in paper so they stay warm until the next drop.

Soften 2 chopped eschalots and crushed garlic in butter in a big pot. Add 1kg cleaned mussels and 200ml white wine, cover and steam for 5 minutes until open. Toss through chopped parsley and a knob of butter and serve with crusty bread to mop up.

w.note: the mess hall at the forward base
w.how: Soak 200g chopped dates in boiling water with a pinch of bicarb. Cream 60g butter with 150g brown sugar, add 2 eggs, the dates and 175g self-raising flour. Bake at 180C for 35 minutes. Pour over hot sauce of butter, brown sugar and cream and serve with custard.
